name: Ari Lerner
headline: Bitmover • Founder • Systems Architect • Mathematics, infrastructure, and cybersecurity

narrative.hook: Thirty years in, I still build the hard part myself: the mathematics, the runtime, and the security boundary.
narrative.body:
I have spent three decades going down rather than sideways — from applications, to platforms, to the runtimes and formal structures underneath them. Today that means proving mathematics in Lean 4 and compiling it into Rust that runs on bare metal, and designing security boundaries strong enough to contain autonomous AI agents executing untrusted code.

I studied theoretical mathematics with an emphasis on harmonics, computer science, and theater arts — which turned out to be the exact toolkit for this work: resonance algebras underneath the runtime, and the ability to stand in front of a room and make people care about them. Along the way I built a developer-education company to 50K+ students, wrote ten books, and shipped open source developers actually run.

experience.title: Founder
highlights: Authored the mathematical core — a 12,288-element (48×256) prime-structure boundary with a 96-class resonance algebra, unity constraints, and conservation invariants — formalized in Lean 4 and exported over a stable C ABI to Rust, Go, Python, and Node.

Co-inventor on the patent-pending inference method — "Systems and Methods for Holographic Computing", U.S. provisional filed February 2026: identical work is content-addressed once and never recomputed, and finite-domain functions dispatch as O(1) lookup tables — ~28× on bf16 GELU, bit-identical.

Invented a transformerless inference path: transformer language models cross-compiled into multiplication-free artifacts whose entire runtime arithmetic is add / shift / xor / compare / table-read, at 28.1× compression and a certified residual.
Built hologram-ai, compiling Hugging Face models into self-contained applications with deterministic CPU-only inference — no MatMul, no GPU, no ONNX, no network at runtime.

Contribute to MIT's Project NANDA (Networked Agents and Decentralized AI): authored the UOR-NANDA interoperability profile inside the UOR Standards Program and presented "The Object Internet" at NANDA 2026.

experience.title: Founder
highlights: Architected MVM, a security-first microVM platform where workloads boot their own kernel with no guest network device at all — the host originates every connection, so default-deny egress is mechanically enforced rather than documented.

Defined 18 numbered security claims — signed execution plans, chain-signed audit logs, dm-verity boot, sealed production images — each bound to executable witnesses so a claim cannot regress without failing CI.
Built secret substitution and PII redaction over vsock so raw credentials never reach the guest, including detection of secrets split across frame boundaries.
Designed the AI-agent containment surface: run-shaped capability grants that give autonomous agents somewhere to execute model-generated code without trusting it.
Built RoboRef, a real-time computer vision system for youth sports — referee and gameplay tracking with autonomous camera control and low-latency edge inference.

projects.name: Hologram — O(1) Neural Inference
projects.desc: Neural network inference in constant time via precomputed lookup tables and KV-dispatch: identical work is content-addressed once and never recomputed. Finite-domain functions dispatch as O(1) tables — ~28× on bf16 GELU, bit-identical — and the same archive runs on x86_64, WebAssembly, and ARM bare metal.

projects.name: F₁ — Lean 4 Arithmetic Geometry
projects.desc: A Lean 4 research base mechanizing the fibre square Spec Z × Spec Z over F₁, whose Hodge-index positivity would yield the Riemann Hypothesis. The geometry is formalized and machine-checked; RH itself is stated as open, not claimed.

projects.name: UOR — uor.foundation
projects.desc: The Universal Object Reference framework: a formal ontology for content-addressed, symmetric, multi-metric object spaces with algebraic structure over Z/(2ⁿ)Z — 16 namespaces, 213 classes, 438 properties — generated into typed Rust traits, JSON-LD, and Turtle from one source of truth. Ships with PRISM, a universal coordinate system for information.

projects.name: MVM — Security-First MicroVM Platform
projects.desc: Runs OCI images, Nix flakes, or decorated functions in hardware-isolated microVMs with no guest NIC at all. Default-deny egress, signed execution plans, chain-signed audit logs, dm-verity boot, and secret substitution over vsock — 18 claims, each enforced by CI rather than documentation.

projects.name: AgentZero
projects.desc: A fast, small, secure AI agent runtime in Rust — deny-by-default policies, encrypted vault, PII redaction, full audit trails, and a WASM plugin sandbox. Your agents, your data, your rules: enforced, not promised.

projects.name: transformerless / uor-r4
projects.desc: Cross-compiles a transformer LLM into a table-native, certifiable artifact: the runtime's entire arithmetic interface is add/shift/xor/compare/table-read. 28.1× compression at a certified residual, with a machine-checked op census on every run.
